claim: Multi-agent debate systems suffer from a 'cognitive islands' problem where agents with limited, different knowledge backgrounds can reach consistent but factually wrong consensus; a shared retrieval knowledge pool mitigates this by connecting agents' knowledge spaces.
stance_target: necessity of shared/external evidence grounding in multi-agent adversarial review architectures to prevent correlated hallucination
quoted_support: It is challenging to make various agents perform right and highly consistent cognition due to their limited and different knowledge backgrounds (i.e., cognitive islands), which hinders the search for the optimal solution.

claim: MADKE running on the open-source Qwen1.5-72B-Chat model surpasses GPT-4 by +1.26% on average across six benchmark datasets when using knowledge-enhanced multi-agent debate.
stance_target: economic argument that multi-agent orchestration architecture can substitute for raw single-model scale/cost in a software factory
scope_conditions: six NLP benchmark datasets, Qwen1.5-72B-Chat vs GPT-4 backbone comparison
quoted_support: MADKE using Qwen1.5-72B-Chat surpasses GPT-4 by +1.26% on average in six datasets, which validates that our method can help open-source LLMs achieve or even surpass the performance of GPT-4.

claim: MADKE's adaptive knowledge selection allows each agent to independently decide, per debate round, whether to use retrieved external knowledge or rely on internal reasoning, rather than forcing uniform retrieval.
stance_target: design pattern for selective/adaptive tool use within multi-agent review pipelines
quoted_support: This method allows agents to choose whether to use external knowledge in each conversation round according to their own needs.
